tier_reason: Phoronix is an independent third party and two WebSearch snippets of https://www.phoronix.com/review/amd-aocc-milanx/6 agree on every figure in the record: 56 C/C++ tests, AOCC 3.2 fastest 66% vs GCC 11.2 19.6% and Clang 14.0 14%, geomean about 8% over GCC 11.2 and Clang about 2% over GCC, flags '-O3 -march=native -flto', 2P EPYC 7773X, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. The page, the OpenBenchmarking result 2204117-NE-EPYC7773X86 and amd.com were all EGRESS_BLOCKED, so this is snippet-only verification and stays at C; it would qualify for B, or A from the public Phoronix Test Suite profiles plus stated compilers, flags and CPU, once the article or the result file is opened.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: AOCC 3.2 (based on upstream LLVM/Clang 13.0) vs GCC 11.2 and LLVM Clang 14.0, the Ubuntu 22.04 LTS default packages; CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS '-O3 -march=native -flto' for all three (per search snippets of the article, page not opened)
corrections.hardware: 2P AMD EPYC 7773X (Milan-X, Zen 3, 1.5 GB L3 in total, 128 cores / 256 threads), Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
corrections.license: Proprietary AMD EULA, binary-only (the Spack recipe declares LicenseRef-AMD-Proprietary, redistribute(source=False, binary=False) and needs +license-agreed)
corrections.stars_or_usage: AMD's vendor C/C++/Fortran compiler for Zen CPUs, free to download under the EULA; packaged in Spack by AMD's amd-toolchain-support account (versions 3.2.0 to 5.2.0, 5.2.0 added 2026-05-29); search results show HPC-center docs (Purdue RCAC) and a Gentoo wiki page
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: phoronix.com, openbenchmarking.org and amd.com are EGRESS_BLOCKED here, so the 8% geomean, the 66%/19.6%/14% win shares, the flags and the CPU come from two WebSearch summaries of the Phoronix article, not from the opened page; the per-test results (OpenBenchmarking 2204117-NE-EPYC7773X86) were not seen. Single 2022 run on one dual-socket Zen 3 server; AOCC 3.2 is based on LLVM 13.0, older than the Clang 14.0 it beat, and both GCC 11.2 and Clang 14 are now several releases old. The gain is modest (about 8% geomean, with GCC or Clang fastest in about a third of the tests) and tuned for AMD Zen; with -march=native the comparison includes each compiler's znver3 tuning. A later Phoronix article (AOCC 4.0, Ryzen 9 7950X, 190 tests, snippet only) reports about 4% geomean over GCC 12.2 with AOCC first in about 55% of tests; the AOCC 5.0 article on 2P EPYC 9755 (Zen 5, LLVM 17.0.6 base) shows clear wins in some workloads and minimal differences from upstream Clang in others, with no geomean visible in snippets. Binary-only under an AMD EULA: no source for AMD's LLVM changes, cannot be redistributed or packaged by distributions, x86-64 Linux only.

notes: Keep as a reference entry: AOCC is a widely deployed, actively released vendor compiler (5.1.0 added to Spack 2026-01-09, 5.2.0 on 2026-05-29) with independent third-party numbers against GCC across two Phoronix articles, and the catalog already keeps binary-only references (CKTSO, HYLU, UDisk); usability reference and has_code false are correct.
